items.title: GWTC-5.0 webinar
items.text: We organized an online webinar to present and discuss the recent GWTC-5.0 papers, "Overview of GWTC-5.0: Introduction/Methods/Results". Check out the recording on YouTube.

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We proposed a novel method for a fast targeted GW search using GstLAL pipeline by incorporating information of electromagnetic emission while maintaining a low computational cost.

items.title: GWTC-5.0 release!
items.text: I led an editorial team for Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog-5.0 Results paper, and it was released together with public data.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Scalable matched-filtering pipeline for gravitational-wave searches of compact binary mergers" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We summarized new methods we developed in the GstLAL pipeline for the upcoming Gravitational Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-4).

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We introduced a new framework to reuse GstLAL's online search and compared with its offline configuration, paving a way to the new regime of GW CBC searches.

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We present a scalable gravitational-wave search pipeline (SGNL) which modernizes the GstLAL pipeline with the PyTorch framework, enabling flexible execution on CPUs and GPUs.

items.title: Start a new position!
items.text: I am joining Nevada Center for Astrophysics (NCfA) at University of Nevada, Las Vegas, as a Postdoctoral Fellow.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Searching for gravitational-wave signals from precessing black hole binaries with the GstLAL pipeline" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We searched for precessing black hole binaries in the third observing run using the GstLAL detection pipeline. Though we didn't find new events, this shows good promise to make new discoveries in the future.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Template bank for compact binary mergers in the fourth observing run of Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Performance of the low-latency GstLAL inspiral search towards LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA’s fourth observing run" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Rapid localization and inference on compact binary coalescences with the Advanced LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA gravitational-wave detector network" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Extension of the Bayesian searches for anisotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background with nontensorial polarizations" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Method for removing signal contamination during significance estimation of a GstLAL analysis" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We extended the Bayesian searches for anisotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background to include non-GR polarizations.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "Improved ranking statistics of the GstLAL inspiral search for compact binary coalescences" has been published in Physical Review D.

items.title: New paper!
items.text: We developed a rapid parameter estimation for GW signals from a compact binary, using the reduced-order-quadrature technique.

items.title: Journal publication
items.text: The paper "pygwb: A Python-based Library for Gravitational-wave Background Searches" has been published in The Astrophysical Journal.

about.title: About Me
about.body:
I am Leo Tsukada, a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Nevada Center for Astrophysics at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV). Previously, I was an Assistant Research Professor in the Institute for Gravitation and the Cosmos at the Pennsylvania State University. I received my Ph.D. in Physics from the University of Tokyo (RESCEU). I am also a member of the LIGO Scientific Collaboration, and my research interest is mainly in the data analysis of gravitational waves.

In particular, I have been interested in two kinds of gravitational-wave signals: the low-latency detection of gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences, and the stochastic gravitational-wave background. Please visit the Research page for more details.

I work closely with a LIGO group led by Prof. Carl-Johan Haster at UNLV, where we work on various projects related to gravitational-wave detection and inference.
